label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
I didn’t want to respond to @Kavya’s post with an argument in the comments. But since people in our Foundry91 batch know it’s about DabbaDost, I want to own what I got wrong and clear up a few things.

Kavya and I are both from Foundry91 cohort 4. Before our demo day in March 2026, she sat with me in the Koramangala office until 1 am fixing a Razorpay webhook mess. She had plenty of her own work to do, but she stayed. I haven’t forgotten that, and I have a lot of respect for her and what she’s building at SitterNest.

Earlier this month, two engineers from SitterNest joined DabbaDost. I knew where they worked from day one. I should have called Kavya before making the offers, not after they were accepted. That’s on me. I understand why hearing about it at that stage would have felt bad, especially coming from someone in the same cohort.

I also want to put the facts out there, because some details in the post aren’t right:

- We posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 September. It was open to anyone.
- One person applied on 19 September. The other came through his referral about two weeks later. Nobody from my side DMed either of them.
- The offers were at 22% above their current CTC, not 40%. Both joined on 3 November.
- We do have an ESOP pool. It’s small, but it’s real and has been on paper since January.

After the second offer was accepted, I messaged Kavya on WhatsApp. She read it but didn’t reply. I should have reached out sooner, and I wish I’d handled that conversation better.

We’re 11 startups in a batch, hiring from a small pool across HSR and Koramangala. This is going to come up again. Maybe we can agree on a simple cohort rule: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer.

I’m not posting this to fight with Kavya or take away from how she feels. I wanted to correct the record without involving the two people who joined us; they didn’t ask to be part of a public discussion.

Kavya, coffee or a call is open this week, whenever you’re comfortable. I’d rather talk to you directly.
